neighbours.label: The locating word right after a comparative or superlative of degree, saying where or when the quality peaks ('strongest near', 'greatest during', 'heaviest along'); quiet for the same prepositions without a graded comparison
fire: Tides are highest near the mouth of the estuary.
Noise levels are greatest during the evening rush hour.
The current is strongest near the outer bank of the river.
Erosion is most severe along the unprotected northern shore.
Pollen counts tend to be higher during dry, windy afternoons.
Snow lies deepest near the top of the pass.
The smell of smoke was stronger directly behind the kitchen.
Demand for electricity is heaviest during the coldest weeks of January.
quiet: We camped near the mouth of the estuary.
The road is closed during the evening rush hour.
A heron stood near the outer bank of the river.
They walked along the unprotected northern shore.
The festival is held during dry, windy afternoons in March.
A small hut stands near the top of the pass.
The bins are kept directly behind the kitchen.
The lake freezes during the coldest weeks of January.

notes: Card: ' near', ' at', ' during', ' directly', ' mid' after 'strongest', 'greatest', 'better'. Probe: 'worse near' 0.48, 'greatest during' 0.34, 'heaviest along' 0.28, 'more common among' 0.18; same prepositions without a comparison 0.01-0.04; 'strongest in' 0.02.
